title: Hippogriff Logistics LLM routing & private deploy scratchpad
body:
Call 2025-11-03 (recorded) - quick capture + actions
Participants: Aisha (RW), Marcus (RW), Sofia (RW), Tom R. (Hippogriff CTO), Priya K. (Hippogriff infra lead)

High-level ask
- Hippogriff wants an internal assistant for routing ops and ETA predictions integrated into their dispatch console.
- MUST run in their colo / VPC (data residency + low egress) with private control plane.
- Target: 99.9% availability for inference endpoints during business hours (6am-10pm local), <200ms p95 per-request for short responses (~<=120 tokens).
- Throughput: bursts to 120 reqs/min, steady 20–40 reqs/min. Spiky daytime pattern.
- Security: SOC2-ish, customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM), audit logs shipped to their Splunk cluster.

Notes / constraints (verbatim-ish)
- "Can't have anything touch public hosted API for PII logs" — they require private deployment.
- Latency sensitivity: UI will time out after 400ms; they want conservative headroom so fallbacks are important.
- They prefer smaller model (13B class) with quantization if quality is acceptable. Budget target = < $0.03 / inference request on average (rough).
- Model answers are often used to seed planner; hallucinations cause rework downstream — need guardrails and evals for critical prompts.

Technical gotchas we flagged
- KV cache sizing: some queries include 2–3 minute running context (many short messages). If we allow long prefix caching, GPU memory pressure may increase. Need to measure median context length + tail.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: they want immediate partial responders in the UI but also post-processing that relies on full response. Consider streaming with reassembly + idempotency.
- Tokenization differences: their dataset includes a lot of domain-specific codes (route IDs like R-9F8). Need to confirm tokenizer OOV behavior for chosen model.
- Networking: colo -> private control plane handshake. We must produce a network diagram and IP allowlist for their security team.
- Logging retention: they want short-term debug logs (14d) and long-term redacted metrics only. Need support for configurable retention / automatic redaction.
- Fallback policy: they asked about automatic fallback to a hosted smaller model in case local capacity exhausted. This is allowed only if the fallback path is approved and data is redacted/encrypted — likely blocked. Clarify checklist with legal.

Preliminary architecture sketch (notes to self)
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) with Redwood private control plane (managed XFR).
- Inference nodes in their colo (baremetal or cloud region) with Dedicated-like pool pinned to their account. Reserve 2 GPUs (A100/80GB or equivalent) initially; scale to 4 for weekends and growth.
- Smart routing policy: route to onprem pool first; if capacity saturated and fallback allowed, route to Redwood Hosted via scrubber service; otherwise queue with fast fail + client backoff.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for repeated context (last 30s window). Tune eviction policy per observed context distribution.

Open questions to resolve (assign)
- Priya: confirm network topology and whether direct peering or VPN — get diagram + firewall rules by 2025-11-10.
- Legal/Security: confirm whether any fallback to hosted is permitted and what data redaction standard is required (obfuscate PII vs remove entire payload) — due 2025-11-12.
- Marcus: run quick tokenization experiment with candidate models (Llama2-13b, Mistral-instruct-13b, Red-13b-v1) on sample routing messages; report OOV / token size distribution by 2025-11-07.
- Aisha: produce SLO proposal with conservative p95 and burst handling (queue behavior + circuit breaker settings) — draft by 2025-11-09.

Action items (concrete)
- Produce two short docs for Priya: (1) network/IP allowlist + minimal ports; (2) deployment topology options (baremetal vs cloud colo) — owner Aisha — ETA 2025-11-06.
- Quick perf bench: Marcus to spin a local dedicated job reproducing Hippogriff payload distribution (use sample logs they shared) and measure p95 token latency for chosen quantized models. Capture results as CSV and short summary. ETA 2025-11-11.
- Eval plan: Sofia to draft prompt/eval set focusing on hallucination and safety for dispatch-critical queries. Include ~40 golden examples and failure modes. ETA 2025-11-14.
- Meeting with security/legal: schedule follow-up to confirm fallback and logging constraints; Priya to invite their security lead + our security eng (Diego) — target week of 2025-11-10.

Quick risk register (notes)
- Risk: Onprem GPUs unavailable / procurement delays. Mitigation: temporary dedicated capacity in nearest public region with strict redaction — but note legal risk.
- Risk: Model hallucination causes bad dispatch action. Mitigation: conservative guardrail layer (classifier + heuristics) and human-in-loop for risky suggestions.

Prompt engineering gotchas (observed)
- Ship codes often appear as natural language ("arrive 9F8") vs structured; model may paraphrase IDs. Need canonicalization step post-response.
- Responses that include probabilities/confidence are helpful; encourage explicit "confidence" tokens from model via constrained output format.

Notes to self (text stream)
- Keep Hippogriff as high-touch PoC: they'll likely convert if latency & cost align. Emphasize ability to pin model versions and predictable bursts.
- Avoid promising hosted fallback until legal signs off. Preface proposals with "if fallback approved" clauses.

Next meeting: scheduled 2025-11-17 10:00 PT (follow-up architecture + bench results).

Misc references / snippets
- Sample request example from them (sanitized): 
  { user_id: "u-122", route_id: "R-9F8", last_events: ["delayed 10m", "gate change"], constraints: { hazardous: false } }
- Performance targets: p95 <= 200ms for generation <=120 tokens; aim p50 <= 80ms.

End scratchpad.

(Will convert key items into a short PoC brief after Marcus bench + Priya network diagram. — A.)
